facts.fact: Sardar Patel, as Deputy PM and Home Minister, led the integration of the princely states.
V.P. Menon was the civil servant who assisted Patel.
India in 1947 had about 565 princely states.
Each state could join India, join Pakistan or remain independent.
The Instrument of Accession initially ceded defence, external affairs and communications.
A Standstill Agreement kept existing arrangements running while accession was negotiated.
British paramountcy over the states lapsed at independence.
Junagadh joined India through a plebiscite in February 1948.
Hyderabad was integrated by Operation Polo (1948).
The Razakars of Kasim Razvi resisted accession in Hyderabad.
Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947.
Article 370 gave Jammu & Kashmir special status.
Part B states were former princely states under a Rajpramukh.
The Dhar Commission (1948) rejected language as the basis of reorganisation.
The JVP Committee comprised Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
The Fazl Ali Commission accepted language as a factor but rejected 'one language–one state'.
The SRC recommended 16 states and 3 Union Territories.
K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru were the other members of the SRC.
The SRA 1956 created 14 states and 6 Union Territories.
The SRA 1956 was implemented with the 7th Constitutional Amendment.
Andhra State (1953) was the first state formed on a linguistic basis, with Kurnool as capital.
Andhra State followed the death of Potti Sreeramulu after a fast-unto-death.
Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under the Gentlemen's Agreement.
Telangana became the 29th state in 2014.
Goa was liberated by Operation Vijay in 1961.
The French enclaves were transferred de facto in 1954 and by treaty ratified in 1962.
Partition caused one of the largest mass migrations in history.
A Ministry of Rehabilitation resettled refugees.
India became a republic on 26 January 1950.
Air India was nationalised in 1953, the Imperial Bank became SBI in 1955, Kerala got a Communist government in 1957, Goa joined in 1961.
The Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1948) was founded by Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta.
Privy purses were abolished by the 26th Amendment (1971).
Sikkim became the 22nd state through the 36th Amendment (1975).
E.M.S. Namboodiripad headed the first elected Communist state government (Kerala, 1957).
Patel's success earned him the title 'Iron Man of India'.
The States Department was set up on 5 July 1947 with Patel as minister and V.P. Menon as secretary.
Mountbatten urged the princes to accede in his address to the Chamber of Princes on 25 July 1947.
V.P. Menon counted 562 princely states; most textbooks round it to about 565.
By 15 August 1947 all the states within India's borders had acceded except Junagadh, Hyderabad and Jammu and Kashmir.
Travancore's Dewan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer declared independence (June 1947); after an attack on him the state acceded in late July 1947.
Maharaja Hanwant Singh of Jodhpur negotiated with Jinnah before acceding to India in August 1947.
Nawab Hamidullah Khan of Bhopal resisted, acceded in 1947, and Bhopal was taken over as a Chief Commissioner's province on 1 June 1949.
Banganapalle, a small Muslim-ruled state in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, was merged into Madras Province in February 1948.
Pudukkottai merged into Madras Province in March 1948.
Mysore acceded in August 1947; its Maharaja Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar became Rajpramukh (1950–56).
The Nawab of Junagadh, Mahabat Khan III, announced accession to Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
Junagadh's Dewan was Shah Nawaz Bhutto, father of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
A provisional government in exile, the Arzi Hukumat, was set up by Samaldas Gandhi (September 1947).
India took over the administration of Junagadh on 9 November 1947; the plebiscite of 20 February 1948 went overwhelmingly for India.
The last Nizam of Hyderabad was Mir Osman Ali Khan.
Hyderabad signed a one-year Standstill Agreement with India on 29 November 1947.
K.M. Munshi was India's Agent-General in Hyderabad (1948).
Mir Laik Ali was the Nizam's last Prime Minister.
The Razakars were the militia of the Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen led by Kasim Razvi.
Operation Polo lasted from 13 to 17 September 1948; the Nizam surrendered on 17 September.
Major-General J.N. Chaudhuri became Military Governor of Hyderabad after Operation Polo.
M.K. Vellodi, a civil servant, was made Chief Minister of Hyderabad State in 1950.
The Nizam was made Rajpramukh of Hyderabad State (1950–56).
17 September is marked as Hyderabad Liberation Day.
Pakistani tribal raiders invaded Kashmir on 22 October 1947.
Mountbatten accepted the accession on 27 October 1947, when Indian troops were flown into Srinagar.
India referred the Kashmir question to the UN Security Council on 1 January 1948.
A UN-brokered ceasefire in Kashmir took effect on 1 January 1949.
Sheikh Abdullah headed the emergency administration of Jammu and Kashmir (1947) and became its Prime Minister in 1948.
Article 370 was made inoperative on 5 August 2019; J&K and Ladakh became Union Territories on 31 October 2019.
The Orissa (Eastern) states were merged into Orissa province on 1 January 1948 — the first mergers.
The Chhattisgarh states were merged into the Central Provinces on 1 January 1948.
Saurashtra (United State of Kathiawar) was the first union of states, formed on 15 February 1948.
The Matsya Union (Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli) was formed in March 1948.
Vindhya Pradesh (Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand states, capital Rewa) was formed in April 1948.
Madhya Bharat (Gwalior, Indore and the Malwa states) was formed in May 1948.
PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) was formed on 15 July 1948.
Rajasthan was built up in stages; Greater Rajasthan was inaugurated on 30 March 1949 (Rajasthan Day).
Travancore-Cochin was formed by uniting the two states on 1 July 1949.
Himachal Pradesh was created on 15 April 1948 from about 30 hill states as a Chief Commissioner's province.
Baroda was merged into Bombay Province on 1 May 1949.
Cooch Behar acceded in 1949 and became part of West Bengal on 1 January 1950.
Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh signed the Manipur Merger Agreement at Shillong on 21 September 1949; it took effect on 15 October 1949.
Tripura merged with India on 15 October 1949 under Regent Maharani Kanchan Prabha Devi.
Bilaspur was a Part C state from 1950 and was merged into Himachal Pradesh in 1954.
Privy purses to the former rulers were guaranteed by Articles 291 and 362 of the Constitution.
The Supreme Court struck down the 1970 derecognition of the princes in Madhav Rao Scindia v. Union of India (1970), leading to the 26th Amendment.
The 7th Amendment (1956) abolished the office of Rajpramukh along with the Part A/B/C/D scheme.
Chandernagore voted to join India in a 1949 referendum, was transferred de facto in 1950 and merged with West Bengal in 1954.
The Kizhoor referendum (18 October 1954) led to the de facto transfer of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam on 1 November 1954.
The 14th Amendment (1962) made Pondicherry a Union Territory after the de jure transfer of 16 August 1962.
Yanam, a former French settlement surrounded by Andhra Pradesh (Kakinada area), is a district of Puducherry UT.
Operation Vijay (18–19 December 1961) ended Portuguese rule; 19 December is Goa Liberation Day.
The 12th Amendment (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory.
In the Goa Opinion Poll of 16 January 1967 Goans voted against merging with Maharashtra.
Goa became the 25th state on 30 May 1987 (56th Amendment); Daman and Diu stayed a Union Territory.
Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed from the Portuguese by volunteers in 1954 and made a Union Territory by the 10th Amendment (1961).
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into one Union Territory on 26 January 2020.
The 35th Amendment (1974) made Sikkim an "associate state" of India.
After a referendum in April 1975 abolished the Chogyal's monarchy, Sikkim became the 22nd state on 16 May 1975.
Kazi Lhendup Dorji was the first Chief Minister of the state of Sikkim.
The Linguistic Provinces Commission under S.K. Dhar was appointed by the Constituent Assembly President in June 1948.
The JVP Committee was set up at the Jaipur Congress (December 1948) and reported in April 1949.
The States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in December 1953 and reported on 30 September 1955.
The SRC weighed four factors: unity and security of India, linguistic and cultural homogeneity, financial and administrative viability, and planning/welfare.
The States Reorganisation Act took effect on 1 November 1956.
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 created five Zonal Councils — Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern.
Kerala was formed on 1 November 1956 by joining Travancore-Cochin with Malabar.
The SRA kept Bombay as a large bilingual state of Marathi and Gujarati speakers.
The Bombay Reorganisation Act split Bombay into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
The Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat (Indulal Yagnik) movements forced the 1960 split.
Nagaland became a state on 1 December 1963 (13th Amendment, Article 371A).
The Shah Commission (1966) drew the Punjab–Haryana boundary; Haryana was formed on 1 November 1966.
The Punjabi Suba movement was led by Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh.
Himachal Pradesh became a full state on 25 January 1971.
Meghalaya became an autonomous state within Assam in 1970 (22nd Amendment) and a full state in 1972.
Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states on 21 January 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
Mizoram became a state on 20 February 1987 after the Mizo Accord (1986) with Laldenga (53rd Amendment).
Arunachal Pradesh also became a state on 20 February 1987 (55th Amendment).
In November 2000 Chhattisgarh (1 Nov), Uttaranchal/Uttarakhand (9 Nov) and Jharkhand (15 Nov) became the 26th, 27th and 28th states.
Uttarakhand was formed on 9 November 2000 as Uttaranchal and renamed in 2007.
Chhattisgarh, carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000, was the 26th state.
Madras State was renamed Tamil Nadu in 1969, and Mysore was renamed Karnataka in 1973.
The 69th Amendment (1991) gave Delhi the status of the National Capital Territory with a legislature.
In the first Council of Ministers Nehru held External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations and Scientific Research.
Patel held Home Affairs, States, and Information and Broadcasting.
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the first Education Minister.
R.K. Shanmukham Chetty was the first Finance Minister.
Sardar Baldev Singh was the first Defence Minister.
John Mathai held Railways and Transport.
Jagjivan Ram was the first Labour Minister.
Rajkumari Amrit Kaur was the first Health Minister.
Rafi Ahmed Kidwai held Communications.
C.H. Bhabha held Commerce.
N.V. Gadgil held Works, Mines and Power.
Jairamdas Daulatram held Food and Agriculture.
K.C. Neogy held Relief and Rehabilitation.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee (Hindu Mahasabha) held Industries and Supplies and resigned in April 1950.
N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar was a minister without portfolio (link with the East Punjab government and Kashmir affairs).
C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Mountbatten on 21 June 1948 as the first and last Indian Governor-General.
Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions; his award was published on 17 August 1947.
The Nehru–Liaquat Pact (Delhi Pact) of 8 April 1950 dealt with the protection of minorities in both countries.
